# Claude Code Plugins

A plugin is a folder that adds skills, agents, hooks, or MCP servers to Claude Code.
A marketplace is a list of plugins that you can install.
For example, `claude plugin install my-plugin@my-marketplace` installs a plugin from a marketplace.

## Marks

| Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| ✅ | A page of the [Claude Code docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) names it. |
| 🔍 | Only the Claude Code bundle names it. No docs page does. |
| ⚠️ | The docs and the bundle differ. The row says how. |
| 🧪 | It works only behind a flag, a plan, or a server-side switch. The row says which. |
| ❌ | It is removed or does nothing in `2.1.303`. |

## Overview

- A plugin is a folder with an optional `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.
  Its parts are skills, commands, agents, hooks, MCP servers, LSP servers, monitors, output styles, workflows, themes, `bin/`, and mods.
- A marketplace lists plugins in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.
- A plugin id is `name@marketplace`.
  Special marketplaces: `inline` (session flags), `builtin`, `skills-dir`, `synced`.
- Enable state is in `enabledPlugins`.
  Scopes are `user`, `project`, `local`, and `managed`.
- Plugin skills are namespaced as `/<plugin>:<skill>`.
  See [Skills and Commands](Claude-Code-Skills-And-Commands).
